changelog: Replace C6 severity to prioritise avoiding splits of determiner/head and required postmodifiers, and to mark markers immediately before punctuation or at the NP tail as milder — addresses the intra-NP ordering bug and the determiner/numeral split check.
findings: When two candidate cuts fall inside the same NP, the prompt misorders them — it sometimes prefers the later NP-tail cut but should prefer an earlier punctuation-separated cut when that preserves a complete clause.
The prompt allows cuts that split a determiner/numeral/pronoun from the noun phrase it heads, breaking NP cohesion.

diagnosis.why: Reweighting C6 made the model more protective of determiner/head and required postmodifier boundaries while at the same time treating markers at NP tails or immediately before punctuation as milder; that moved the top-one/two cut preferences (rank_depth: depth1 down, depth2 up) so some long-latency top cuts improved but many medium-latency cuts (especially ≤7 and ≤5 bins) shifted into intra‑NP positions or split enumerations, producing roughly equal numbers better/worse and a small net drop.
diagnosis.lesson: Keep the stronger protection against splitting determiners/heads and required postmodifiers, but do not so aggressively lower severity for markers at NP tails / before punctuation that intra‑NP cuts and enumeration splits become more likely (test effects per latency bin, esp. ≤7).
